behavior_constraints: Every `mlpipe run` execution writes a JSON run record to `.mlpipe/runs/<unix_timestamp_ms>.json` after completion (success or failure).

Run record contains: run_id (string ms timestamp), pipeline, started_at (ISO 8601 UTC), finished_at (ISO 8601 UTC), duration_ms, status, mode (standard|cv), cv_folds (int or null), no_cache, skipped_stages, stage_summary (per-stage status/cache_hit/duration_ms), cache_stats (hits/misses or null when --no-cache).
Run record filename uses the same Unix timestamp in milliseconds as run_id.
`mlpipe history [--pipeline <name>] [--status <status>] [--limit N]` outputs `{"runs":[...],"count":N}` with each run abbreviated (run_id, pipeline, status, started_at, duration_ms, mode).
History runs sorted by run_id descending (most recent first).
History --limit N returns at most N runs (default: all); --pipeline filters by pipeline name; --status filters by success/failed.

`mlpipe diff <config1.json> <config2.json>` outputs pipeline_name (only if names differ), stages_added, stages_removed, stages_modified (with params_changed/deps_changed/type_changed/inputs_changed shown only when changed), stages_unchanged.
Stages matched by name; modified if type, params, depends_on, or inputs differ; params_changed shows only differing keys.
Diff command reports error via exitError if either config fails to parse.
All prior behaviors (caching, CV, plan, registry, lineage, ensemble, skipping, on_failure) remain unchanged.
entities.summary: Add run-history recording for every `mlpipe run`, a `history` command to query past runs, and a `diff` command to compare two pipeline configurations.

instruction_head:
We need to add pipeline history and auditing capabilities so we can track what happened over time and debug production issues.

## 1. Run History Recording
